legend: Cutaneous involvement by myeloid sarcoma in a patient with a history of acute myeloid leukaemia who presented with an isolated nodular lesion on the right lower back. Diffuse monoblastic infiltrate involves dermis and subcutaneous tissue with sparing of the epidermis (grenz zone). Focally, the neoplastic cells exhibit a single-file pattern of infiltration.
Monoblasts are of medium-large size, with fine chromatin, a distinct nucleolus, and a scant to moderate amount of cytoplasm.

The myeloid blasts have abnormal cytoplasmic NPM1 expression in addition to normal nuclear positivity, indicative of NPM1 mutation. The normal endothelial cells within the vessel have only nuclear-restricted NPM1 expression.

diagnosis: Neoplastic myeloid blast infiltrate, consistent with acute myeloid leukaemia involving skin
legend: Cutaneous involvement by neoplastic myeloid blasts in a patient with acute myeloid leukaemia who presented with a violaceous papular lesion on the left inner thigh. The myeloid blast infiltrate is periadnexal and perivascular and involves the subcutaneous adipose tissue; the epidermis is spared. Given the infiltrate with blasts ≥ 20%, the diagnosis of acute myeloid leukaemia involving skin is most appropriate.
